messages.author: 970bb92277d806ae
messages.subject: Problem with a ideal point estimation model
parts:
Hi,


I'm a newbie and I don't know if I'm doing this right.

I'm trying to run a ideal points model based on "legislators" by Simon Jackman. This model was originally written in WinBUGS and I'm coding it in Stan. 

Unfortunately, my algorithm has got stuck here for hours:

"SAMPLING FOR MODEL '5d63bb8f5de6f7104af8cc8a19924b0d' NOW (CHAIN 1).

Chain 1, Iteration:     1 / 12000 [  0%]  (Warmup)"


I don't know if it is normal or I'm making a mistake with my model (posted below).

Could someone check it?

Guilherme

PS: I have seen there's another post about the same algorithm ('legislators') here ( https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/stan-users/OWyrW9176f8/Z_fY1t2WwM4J ) but I decided to start a new one because I thought my issues were specific.


The complete code: < http://github.com/duarteguilherme/legislators-based/ >

My model is this:

'data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  int<lower=0> L; // legisladores
  int<lower=0> K; // rollcalls
  int<lower=0> jj[N];
  int<lower=0> kk[N];
  int<lower=0, upper=1> y[N];
}
parameters {
  real beta0[K];
  real beta1[K];
  real x[L];
}
transformed parameters {
}

model {
for (i in 1:N){
    y[i] ~ bernoulli(Phi_approx(x[jj[i]]*beta1[kk[i]] - beta0[kk[i]]));
}


for (i in 1:40){ x[i] ~ normal(0,1); }
  for (i in 42:65){ x[i] ~ normal(0,1); }
  for (i in 67:100){ x[i] ~ normal(0,1); }
  beta1 ~ normal(0, 2);
  beta0 ~ normal(0, 2);
  x[41] ~ normal(-1, .0001);
  x[66] ~ normal(1, .0001);
}
'

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Problem with a ideal point estimation model
parts:
You just do something like this:

parameters{
…
vector[L-2] z;
}

transformed parameters {
  vector[L] x;
  for (i in 1:41) x[i] <- z[i];
  for (i in 42:65) x[i] <- z[i-1];
  for (i in 67:100) x[i] <- z[i-2];
  x[41] <- 1;
  x[66] <- -1;
}

model {
  z ~ normal(0,1);
…
}

Or something like that.  I might be mangling the syntax, also this is a bit of an ugly way to do it, but you should get the general idea.
A
